Your business ran a small deficit this period—spending exceeded income by about 2,200 dollars.

Here are the key issues:

Your income is heavily concentrated. Your top client represents over 80 percent of all revenue, and your top three clients account for nearly 95 percent. A loss of any major client would create serious problems. Diversify your revenue streams urgently.

Shopping expenses dominate your spending at 52 percent of total costs. This is your largest controllable category. Review these purchases closely to identify what can be cut or negotiated—this is where you'll find relief.

Your fixed costs (utilities and payroll) are substantial at 45 percent of spending. These are harder to trim, but worth auditing for waste. Your discretionary spending of 34,000 dollars is where most opportunity lies.

On the positive side, you have only four expense categories and four income sources, making your business relatively simple to manage and analyze.

Act now: secure additional revenue clients, scrutinize shopping expenses, and verify your fixed costs are necessary.
